thread:
sanjay: pushed kernel-selector tweak to canary ~10:03 UTC, noticed TTFT (time-to-first-token) up ~8% on /chat-stream route. decode time itself looks flat but kernel_handoff_ms jumped. anyone seen similar? :thinking:

maria: can you paste the probe-runner trace or a small sample? curious if KV cache hit-rate changed or if we're seeing queueing before kernel init.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for kernel-selector:v2 -> 3 hosts (tags: canary).

li: quick prometheus spit for context, trying to correlate queue vs kernel:```sum(rate(runtime_kernel_handoff_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le,route)```also:```
(1 - sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_lookups_total[5m]))) * 100 as "kv_miss_pct"
```kv miss pct on /chat-stream looks normal (~2%).

kevin: my money's on scheduling handoff. v2 changed the microbatch handshake order so sometimes we do a light-weight kernel probe then handoff again -> extra memcpy/serialize. need token-level waterfall to confirm: prequeue -> queue -> handshake -> kernel_exec -> decode.

sanjay: attaching one sample timeline (probe-runner trimmed):```
token0: prequeue 1.2ms | queue 0.8ms | handshake 4.9ms | kernel_exec 2.1ms | decode 0.6ms
token1: prequeue 1.0ms | queue 0.9ms | handshake 8.7ms | kernel_exec 1.9ms | decode 0.5ms
avg(handshake) jumped from 3.1ms -> 7.8ms on canary hosts
```handshake is the outlier.

ursula: ok good find. for observability we should: 1) emit token_attrib with explicit labels: route, model, kernel_variant, handshake_phase (probe|full), and token_index; 2) add a waterfall panel that stacks per-token percentiles (p50/p95) broken into prequeue/queue/handshake/kernel/decode; 3) surface a "handshake amplification" metric = handshake_ms / kernel_exec_ms per-route.

maria: +1. sampling: full token histograms for every 0.5% of traffic and 100% p50/p95 counters. full traces at 0.5-1% to keep storage sane. also we should tag traces with canary=true when rollout active.

li: quick grep shows a fallback path in PR #5126 where we run a kernel_probe() then fall back to another kernel variant if probe fails. the code path does an extra context copy on fallback (alloc + memcpy) — that explains handshake jump.

kevin: nice catch. hypothesis: probe success rate decreased slightly for longer contexts so fallback overhead more frequent on /chat-stream. need to quantify probe success rate and show correlation with handshake_ms. add a metric: kernel_probe_failed_total{route, kernel_variant}.

sanjay: agree. pausing canary now and rolling back kernel-selector:v2 on those hosts. can we also add a lightweight kernel_probe_success gauge and the handshake amplification metric to the per-route dashboard? want to re-run A/B with instrumentation before reintroducing.

ops-bot: canary rollout for kernel-selector:v2 paused by @sanjay. 3 hosts rolled back.

ursula: I'll mock up the dashboard panels this afternoon and add a short doc for how to read the waterfall (p50 vs p95 differences). maria, li — can you own adding the probe success metric + sampling knobs? kevin, can you sketch the metric names you'll need so platform can instrument?

maria: will do — I'll PR a sampler config and add retention notes. sampling note: token_histogram retention 14 days, full-trace retention 7 days for sampled traces.

li: I'll add the probe_success counter: runtime_kernel_probe_success_total and runtime_kernel_probe_failed_total, both labeled by route and kernel_variant. will also emit kernel_variant on token-level counters.

sanjay: thx team. follow-up: once we re-run A/B, let's capture a small set of golden prompts (short/long context) to stress probe path. want to validate handshake amplification metric moves with probe failures. :eyes:
